html:
The Brokopondo Reservoir is a huge artificial lake in the forest of Suriname, made by the Afobaka Dam on the Suriname River, built from 1961 to 1964. It powered an aluminium smelter.

Bauxite, the ore of aluminium, had been mined in Suriname since the 1910s by a subsidiary of the American company Alcoa, and in the Second World War Suriname supplied much of the bauxite of the Allies. The dam was built to turn the ore into aluminium at home. For decades bauxite and aluminium made up most of the country's exports.

The lake drowned the villages of thousands of Saramaka Maroons, who were moved with little say. It became a symbol of their loss of land. Alcoa closed its operations in the 2010s, leaving gold and oil as the main exports, much as oil has in neighbouring Guyana.
sum: The Brokopondo Reservoir is a huge artificial lake in the forest of Suriname, made by the Afobaka Dam on the Suriname River, built from 1961 to 1964. It powered an aluminium smelter.
